name: Basotho Papa le Moroho
description: Papa (a stiff maize porridge) paired with moroho (cooked leafy greens) is the real, everyday backbone of Basotho meals, eaten at least once a day in most households - real technique beats the cornmeal in gradually to build papa's dense, sliceable texture, while the greens are cooked simply with onion and oil, not heavily seasoned.

ingredients_full.note: shredded, standing in for moroho greens

ingredients.note: shredded, standing in for moroho greens

steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring constantly, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick and it pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in the oil 3-4 minutes, then add the cabbage and a splash of water, and simmer 12-15 minutes until tender.
Serve the papa alongside the moroho.

name: Basotho Motoho
description: Motoho, a fermented sorghum porridge, is a beloved Basotho breakfast - real sorghum ferments overnight, developing a genuine sour tang before cooking, and is traditionally served cold, sometimes sweetened with sugar.
steps_detailed: Whisk the sorghum flour with 1.5 cups water into a thin batter.
Cover and let ferment at room temperature 12-24 hours, until it develops a real sour tang.
Bring to a boil, stirring constantly, then reduce heat and simmer 8-10 minutes until thickened.
Chill completely and serve cold, sweetened with sugar if desired.

name: Basotho Likhobe
description: Likhobe, beans and maize kernels stewed together until tender, is a genuine Basotho staple, real technique soaking both the beans and maize overnight so they cook through evenly together.

Add the cowpeas and corn with enough water to cover, and simmer 25-30 minutes until everything is tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick, stew-like consistency.

name: Basotho Lepu
description: Lepu, summer squash and its leaves cooked together, is one of Lesotho's most beloved variations of moroho, real technique cooking the leaves and diced squash together in the same pot rather than separately.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil 3-4 minutes.
Add the squash and spinach with a splash of water, and simmer 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is soft and well combined.

name: Basotho Nyekoe
description: Nyekoe, beans stewed with pumpkin, is a genuine Basotho comfort dish, real technique letting the pumpkin break down and thicken the stew naturally.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Cowpeas (blackeyes), immature seeds, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

Add the pumpkin and enough water to cover, and simmer 20-22 minutes until the pumpkin breaks down and thickens the pot.
Add the cowpeas and simmer 8-10 minutes more to warm through.

name: Basotho Grilled Meat (Nama)
description: Nama, simply grilled meat, is a genuine centerpiece of Basotho meals whenever it's available, real technique keeping the seasoning minimal so the meat's own flavor carries the dish.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the salt and oil.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 12-15 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

description: Roasted green maize cobs are a beloved Basotho snack, traditionally roasted directly in the hot ashes of an open fire in the highlands.

name: Basotho Steamed Bread
description: Basotho steamed bread is real, distinctive in using a genuine steaming technique rather than baking, giving it a real dense, moist crumb.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt with enough water to form a soft dough.
Shape into a small round loaf and steam over simmering water 40-45 minutes until firm and cooked through.

name: Basotho Egg and Papa Breakfast
description: Papa served with eggs is a common Basotho breakfast, real technique frying the eggs simply so they don't compete with the papa's own mild flavor.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick.
Fry the eggs in the oil until cooked to your liking.
Serve the eggs alongside the papa.
